newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM attempts to avert new political crisis.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM attempts to avert new political crisis.

text.p: The prime minister of the Baltic state of Latvia presented a plan to squabbling political parties on Tuesday aimed at averting a looming crisis which has his government on the ropes.
"I have presented a concrete programme (to the coalition parties) on how to overcome the current problems," Prime Minister Andris Shkele told a news conference.
Shkele, a no-nonsense former businessman with no party affiliation, heads an unwieldy seven-party coalition which has lurched from one crisis to another.

Three ministers have resigned in recent months amid allegations of corruption and a fourth, Interior Minister Dainis Turlais, quit after eight children plunged to their deaths at a firefighting show when the basket they were in fell from a crane.

Shkele on Monday demanded the resignation of a fifth cabinet member, Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans, on the grounds that he had violated anti-corruption legislation by holding state and private jobs simultaneously.
Shkele called on the parties to nominate new candidates to fill the vacant posts and proposed an extraordinary session of parliament on August 6 to vote for the new ministers.
He said that the full details of his plan would be made public on Wednesday.
The frequent bouts of political infighting have not prevented Shkele from speeding up market reforms in the small former Soviet republic.
He has rammed a balanced budget through the raucous 100-seat parliament, privatised key state assets and kept a lid on inflation.
